Fix how visualizer menu shows annotation context data & allow selecting it in the ui (and blueprint!) ### Related * Pre-requisite for RR-3840 * this seems far fetched, but when I attacked that issue head-on I learned that annotation context makes this sooo much harder ### What The end goal is to massively simplify complexity of queries in visualizers and get rid of a tons of small bugs & inconsistencies we have today in that area. A stepping stone is to make annotation context less weird and inconsistent (and not up to individual visualizer impls!): if you open the “detect and track objects” (aka Horses) example then you might notice that labels & colors in the ui have nothing to do with what’s on screen and the whole thing doesn’t quite make sense: Before: After: As you can see the UI is now fully aware of annotation context and queries it correctly. This is the tip of the iceberg of this PR! What actually happens is that we pull out annotation context from the individual visualizers and instead **express it as a redirect on the blueprint-resolved-query level** - this makes this _extremely_ similar to what lenses do already there! Effectively annotation context is now handled as a special cross-entity component mapping! -> we can now trivially extend what annotation context does and trivially register more visualizers to use it. All that's needed is to specify which visualizer-component can be set to which annotation-component. There is a subtle, but potentially impactful breaking change hidden in all this: Previously, it was possible to "fine grained" override annotation context provided values by logging store values every now and then - the annotation context took the role of a gap filler. I had a version where I implemented this but it got pretty complex, so instead I went with the breaking change: if for some reason annotation context mapping is enabled, then any gaps will be filled with the Default, but you can never overlay recording values in there. ### Testing Previously added more tests in https://github.com/rerun-io/reality/pull/3124 --------- Source-Ref: f7456d37010569d09c1727b343b3731e625493f4 Co-authored-by: Copilot Autofix powered by AI <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Pipeline v2 (3/8): extract shared SegmentStore from the CPU worker

Part 3 of the PIPELINE_V2.md migration. Stacked on #3053.

## What

This PR is moving some of the reusable code out of `cpu_worker.rs` into
a new file `segment_store.rs` that will be common to both the existing
v1 and the new v2 pipelines. The reason this is necessary is because we
want to have both pipelines available in the follow on PRs so we can do
easy A/B testing. Some testing code was moved to a `test_utils.rs` for
use against both v1 and v2.

It is important when reviewing this code that we do **NOT** recommend
any changes to the v1 pipeline.

The following code is moved unmodified:

- `send_next_row_batch`
- `emit_up_to`

This allows us to re-use the logic of the latest-at semantics that we
will still need going forward in v2.

The following had very light (basically signature and plumbing) changes:

- `store_bytes`
- `gc_up_to_horizon`
- `new`

The following functions were split up

- `flush_incremental` → `flush_incremental_to` + v1 wrapper
- `record_arrival` → `SegmentStore::insert_chunk` +
`CurrentStores::record_arrival`

The new code is:

- IncrementalFlushOutcome struct  — the return-deltas seam
- SegmentStore::flush — 3-line wrapper over `emit_up_to(None, …)`. Old
`CurrentStores::flush` called `emit_up_to` directly; it now delegates,
still taking `mut self` so `Drop` fires right after the last batch

I updated a bunch of functions from `pub(super)` -> `pub` to be
consistent with the recommendations in `CLAUDE.md` and these weren't
exposed beyond the crate anyway.

## Testing

- Existing tests were moved over
- New test: `insert_chunk` tracks `max_arrived_time_max` monotonically,
ignores other timelines.

## Stack

1. #3052
2. #3053
3. **→ this PR**
4. `pipeline_v2` internals
5. executor + driver + bridge + env switch (default off)
6. component-tests A/B configs
7. default-on flip
8. v1 deletion

Stop repainting every frame while chunk fetches are in flight

### Related

* Part of RR-5643

### Clanker details

While any chunk request was pending, `receive_messages` called
`request_repaint` every frame, so the viewer ran at full frame rate for
the whole duration of a download, including background prefetch of
`Similar` chunks that the user is not waiting for.

Now the fetch task requests a repaint after it has fulfilled its
promise, and the per-frame busy repaint is gone.
The promise is fulfilled before the repaint is requested so the frame it
wakes cannot poll it too early.
The fetch task is spawned on the app's `AsyncRuntimeHandle` instead of
`poll_promise::Promise::spawn_async`, which is the same tokio runtime on
native and `spawn_local` on web.

This is also what made `datasets::start_with_segment_fragment_url` flaky
on Windows: the test waits for the required chunks, then
`set_selection_panel_opened` requires the viewer to settle within 4
steps, but background prefetch was still in flight and forced a repaint
every frame (`Harness needed 98 steps to settle`).

The dev panel's server streaming tab no longer refreshes its bandwidth
numbers every frame while idle; it updates on the next repaint.

Fix streams tree staying collapsed when a recording is drawn before its first chunk arrives

### Related

* Part of RR-5643

### What

When a recording's `SetStoreInfo` message is drawn one frame before its
first chunk, the streams tree root `/` is a leaf.
Leaf nodes had `default_open: false`, and egui persists the collapse
state on first draw, so the root stayed collapsed after the entities
arrived.
The user sees an empty streams tree with a collapsed `/` and has to
expand it by hand.

This is what made
`exports_browser::saved_blueprint_roundtrips_through_a_browser_channel`
time out waiting for `test_entity`: the SDK sends blueprint messages
ahead of the batched recording rows, so on the slow browser CI runner
the recording rendered empty for a frame.
The failure dump showed `Entities: 1` in the selection panel but only
`/` in the streams tree.

The root now defaults to open whether or not it has children yet,
matching the rule already used for non-leaf roots.

Reproduced with a time-panel test that renders one frame with only the
store info, then logs an entity and renders again with the same egui
memory:

![Root collapsed on main, open with this
PR](https://static.rerun.io/c9b9539d7879dbf3c05054b183fa5ed11fd1a396_pr3605_streams_root_collapsed.png)

### Testing

`cargo test -p re_time_panel --all-features` passes locally.

Fix missing task labels for LeRobot v3 datasets written with LeRobot 0.5.0+

### What

LeRobot `0.5.0` renamed the pandas index of `meta/tasks.parquet` from
unnamed to `task`, so the string column is now called `task` instead of
`__index_level_0__`.

The v3 importer looked up the old name only, inside a `filter_map` that
swallowed the miss, so every dataset written or converted with LeRobot ≥
0.5.0 silently lost its `/task` entity 😱

So this PR:

* The tasks loader now accepts `task` and falls back to
`__index_level_0__`.
* Warn once when the loaded task count disagrees with `total_tasks` in
`info.json`, and when a frame references a `task_index` that is not
defined.
* The `v30_apple_storage` test fixture's `tasks.parquet` is rewritten in
the current LeRobot format, so the existing schema snapshot now covers
the new layout.

Source-Ref: 9cb8554608c64a7f0c7367bcb9bff222546abf54

Decode the RRD footer once per `RrdReader` instead of once per `store()`

### What

`RrdReaderInternal.store()` re-read and decoded the whole RRD footer on
every call.
The footer holds one manifest per store, so opening one store cost
`O(N)` in the number of stores, and opening all of them cost `O(N^2)`.
This was especially noticeable on combined recordings such as LeRobot
imports, where every episode is its own store. E.g. splitting a
1693-episode dataset spent `~355s` decoding footers versus `~17s` of
actual chunk work 😬

The reader now holds the decoded footer for its lifetime, which for a
many-store RRD is one manifest per store.
This was already being decoded per call, so peak memory is unchanged and
steady-state memory is bounded by a single footer.

Measured on a synthetic 1000-store RRD:

| step               | before  | after   |
| ------------------ | ------- | ------- |
| open reader        | 89 ms   | 86 ms   |
| enumerate stores   | 85 ms   | 0.3 ms  |
| `store()` per call | 87.6 ms | 0.08 ms |

Part 2 of the PIPELINE_V2.md migration.

## What

- **Code motion**: When we get to the V2 version of the pipeline, we
will end up removing the `io_loop` file. Some of the code in that file
is useful to both V1 and V2, so we move a variety of functions *without
modification* to the file `fetch_plan.rs` — with one exception, noted
below.
- **Behavior change**: each segment's chunk-info rows are now
stable-sorted by `{filtered_index}:start` before packing. Static chunks
go first and then all remaining rows are in ascending order.
- **The one modified function**: `split_large_segments` now slices
instead of gathering. It only ever groups consecutive rows, so every
sub-batch is a contiguous range and `RecordBatch::slice` just adjusts
per-column offsets rather than copying. On `main` that path made one
full copy pass per over-target segment; now the sort's `take` makes that
pass and the split makes none, so the copy cost is break-even for
over-target segments. Slicing is infallible, so the function no longer
returns `ApiResult` or takes an `origin`.

## Why the sort lands here, in the live v1 path

The v2 plan-cursor watermark derives each segment's safe horizon from
plan position, which is only sound if plan order equals `time_min` order
— today server row order within a segment is arbitrary. v1 is
delivery-order tolerant (the per-entity `SegmentChunkManifest` exists
for exactly that), so v1 correctness is unaffected. Note it is not
purely an ordering change though: for segments over the byte target,
`split_large_segments` cuts sub-batches on time boundaries instead of
the server's row order, so *which* chunks share a `FetchChunks` request
changes. Since range merging in `fetch_batch_via_direct_urls` can only
merge byte-adjacent chunks that landed in the same request, and only
within a single layer URL, this could shift the direct-fetch merge ratio
in either direction. The existing `direct_original_ranges` /
`direct_merged_ranges` analytics are the signal to watch; worth an A/B
on a multi-layer dataset in stack item 6.

Static/null-start-first placement is deliberate: v2's cursor gates all
emission on those chunks (closing a latent gap where a late-arriving
static chunk misses already-emitted rows).

## Testing

- New `fetch_plan` tests: temporal ordering, static/null-first,
stability, monotone `:start` across large-segment sub-batch boundaries,
order preserved across multi-segment and mixed-flush packing,
no-timeline/no-column no-ops, and a debug-assert guard that a chunk-info
batch never mixes segments.
- Existing planner/wave tests in `io_loop.rs` unchanged and green (they
pass `None` for the timeline — schema has no `:start` column, sort is a
no-op).
- `cargo nextest run --all-features -p re_datafusion`: 278 passed, 1
skipped.

Introduce server `GetWriteAccessGrant` API

### Related

* Part of RR-2017
* Part of RR-5480

### What

This adds a new `GetWriteAccessGrant` RPC call to our Hub API, which
allows putting files into a _credential-free_ context from which they
_can be accessed_ and registered using the existing catalog registration
APIs. A write access grant can be used to put bytes into a context that
the server understands. For the OSS Server this will be the FileSystem,
for cloud deployments this will be an S3 bucket.

In its current form, the only we to redeem a grant is by using an
`HttpRequest`, which can be understood as a thin (but extensible)
wrapper around the concept of S3 presigned URLs. In the future we can
allow other redemption methods that allow different credential minting
strategies.

The plan is to implement this in all our products and platforms, The
initial scope for those is as follows (note that we don't need
`AccessGrants` at all for catalogs which we know to run locally).

| Product | Access Grant | Redemption method |
|-|-|-|
| Hub | Returns a pre-signed URL for Dataset bucket. | Uploads the data
to S3 using HTTP `PUT`. |
| OSS Server | Returns a credential-free HTTP `PUT` URL. | Uploads the
data through a `PUT` route implemented by the OSS server. |
| Native Viewer catalog | not needed | out-of-band write to FS |
| WASM Viewer catalog   | not needed | out-of-band write to OPFS |

### Testing

I've added a (currently ignored) `re_server` test to show of the initial
API.

### Compatibility

This API is purely additive, so backwards compatible. The actual
implementation on Hub might influence Stack / Bucket configuration
(permissions, CORS, etc.), which should probably configurable via our
portal.

commit.message:
Losslessly compress all non-snapshot PNGs

Ran `oxipng -o max --strip safe` over every tracked PNG outside the
kittest snapshot directories.

**849,568 → 692,254 bytes (-18.5%)** across 13 files.

The biggest wins are files that turned out to be mostly editor metadata
rather than image data — `example.png` was 15 KB of which only 2.3 KB
was actual pixels, the rest EXIF/XMP/ICC:

| file | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `examples/assets/example.png` | 15016 | 2396 | -84% |
| `re_ui/data/logo_dark_mode.png` | 12227 | 2612 | -79% |
| `re_ui/data/logo_light_mode.png` | 12287 | 2669 | -78% |
| `re_viewer/data/app_icon_mac.png` | 270325 | 236396 | -13% |
| `re_viewer/data/app_icon.png` | 99475 | 85009 | -15% |
| `re_ui/data/icons/rerun_logo.png` | 83924 | 78151 | -7% |
| `web_viewer/apple-touch-icon.png` (×2) | 47459 | 44961 | -5% |
| droid example images (×2) | 168117 | 142774 | -15% |
| `docs/snippets/…/encoded_depth.png` | 707 |(deleted) | --  |

## This is lossless

- All 13 files decode to **pixel-identical RGBA**, verified at 16-bit
precision (`encoded_depth.png` is 16-bit and stays 16-bit).
- `--strip safe` keeps `iCCP` and `pHYs` and drops only
`zTXt`/`iTXt`/`bKGD`/`tIME`. The embedded ICC profile payload is
byte-identical (same 672 bytes, same SHA-1); oxipng only re-deflates it
and normalises the chunk's profile-name string.
- End-to-end check: regenerating the checked-in YUV fixtures via
`tests/assets/image/generate_yuv_assets.py` from the optimised
`logo_dark_mode.png` produces **byte-identical** `.bin` files.
- `scripts/ci/check_large_files.py` passes.
- The duplicate pairs (`apple-touch-icon.png`) remains byte-identical.
- I looked at the images and they look fine

## Not included

The 1171 kittest snapshot PNGs (60.6 MB) are deliberately excluded
because they're git-LFS tracked, so recompressing them is a 1171-file
LFS churn, and kittest rewrites them unoptimised whenever snapshots are
regenerated.

`ferris.png` is deliberately left uncompressed because
`archetypes/encoded_image` logs its raw bytes, which are pinned by the
backwards-compatibility fixture
`tests/assets/rrd/snippets/archetypes/encoded_image.rrd`.

## Testing
It builds OK. I don't think we have any relevant unit tests.
